newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end weak in pre-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end weak in pre-holiday trade.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended easier but above the key 18,000 points level in thin pre-holiday trade on Thursday, with many players out on the eve of a four-day break for the Chinese and Moslem new years.
"The market didn't go anywhere. It tried to test the low, then the high. But most people are in a Chinese New Year mood," said a trader with a Japanese futures house.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract was down by 230 points to 18,025 at the close after hitting a low of 17,850. Turnover was a light 14,850 lots.
In Tokyo, continued weakness in banking shares after Wednesday's sharp sell-off pulled the Nikkei average down 147.54 points to 18,038.43 by the close.
The dollar's rally towards 124 yen had no impact on Nikkei markets as players had largely factored in a higher dollar, dealers said.
"A lot of people see the dollar going to 125 yen so if it does, it won't catch a lot of people by surprise," said the trader.

He said the March Nikkei was likely to move sideways on Friday as participation would be very thin on SIMEX and players in Osaka would be wary of taking aggressive positions ahead of a meeting of finance ministers from the Group of Seven industrialised nations at the weekend.
